scope: optional Android system TextToSpeech backend for the frozen reader TTS C ABI (READER_TTS_VERSION 0.1.0)
original_delivery_note: the delivery head of the original package branch is unchanged by this review; it is the acceptance commit over fe1eb58e
evidence_doc_commit_note: this commit changes docs/validation/reader-tts-android.json and docs/READER-TTS-ANDROID.md only; the tested source is the SHA above and the final head difference is documentation only

artifacts.purpose: device evidence, installed packages and logs
artifacts.name: reader-tts-android-40170544552-1

review_fixes: stop and request_close end the active request themselves: the accepted request keeps exactly one STOPPED event even when the engine never reports the interrupted utterance, and the handle returns to READY instead of staying STOPPING with every later speak refused as BUSY
a repeated terminal callback for an already ended request is dropped, so onDone plus onStop from one engine cannot produce two terminals for one request
an utterance id that is not decimal or that overflows uint64 is ignored instead of wrapping onto a different request id
callback entries pin the handle for their whole duration, so a destroy that runs next to a late callback cannot free the ring or the lock under it; a callback for a destroyed cookie is refused
reader_tts_voices reported the engine voice id in both id and name; name now carries the localized locale name of the voice
an empty voice_id re-selects the engine default voice instead of inheriting the voice of an earlier explicit request
the per-request text kept for UTF-16 to UTF-8 range conversion is released when a request ends or a new one starts
documented the real thread split (framework init callback on the process main thread, utterance callbacks on engine binder threads, request calls synchronous on the owner thread)

audio.judgements: bytes and container header only, plus the synthesized voice state reported by the engine; no spoken-output quality is claimed

contracts_verified: frozen C ABI 0.1.0 from docs/handoffs/reader-next-wave/tts-contract.md compiled unchanged in an installed consumer
installed prefix consumer: find_package(EXReaderTTSAndroid CONFIG REQUIRED) with EXReaderTTSAndroid::reader_tts
NDK API 26 Debug and Release build with -Wall -Wextra -Werror; host target and API 25 both refused
creating-thread ownership; foreign-thread observe and destroy refused with the pointer kept
strict UTF-8 refusal: overlong, incomplete, encoded surrogate, embedded NUL
rate bounds, request id monotonicity, one active request and BUSY on replacement
byte limit lowering, engine text ceiling and event-queue reserve refusal without truncation
STARTED plus exactly one FINISHED/STOPPED/FAILED per accepted request; a repeated terminal callback for the same request is dropped
stop ends the request itself: exactly one STOPPED, no FINISHED and no FAILED afterwards, request id cleared, handle READY for the next request
close while a request is speaking leaves exactly one STOPPED and then CLOSED
utf8 offsets for RANGE events with the capability bit published only after a real range callback
pause/resume UNSUPPORTED with unchanged state and no CAN_PAUSE capability
voice listing without an engine download: id, localized locale name and BCP 47 language for every installed voice, compared element by element with the engine's own voice objects
an explicit voice id sticks for its request and an empty voice id returns the engine to its default voice
voice list lifetime after handle destroy, null-safe free, voices refused without an engine
request_close idempotent, refuses new work, reaches CLOSED only after the engine release callback
destroy BUSY until CLOSED, then NULL; a callback carrying a destroyed handle cookie is refused and does not reach a later handle
an utterance id above the request id range or not decimal is ignored instead of being wrapped
one long request survives a real Activity recreation (rotation) with one terminal event
long text spoken as bounded chunks with one terminal event each and no byte loss
real synthesizeToFile WAV from the installed engine with matching on-device and published digest
removed-engine run: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, UNAVAILABLE speak/voices and a real refusal path
same-run artifact authentication: name, source, run, attempt, bytes, sha256 and expiry

retained_failures.reason: JNI compile failure: GetStaticMethodID was called without the JNIEnv argument (5 errors)
device step refused before install: the androidTest APK was looked up at outputs/apk/androidTest/debug and Gradle wrote it directly under outputs/apk/androidTest
device job passed with 45 named cases but the summary demanded the enclosing run be completed and successful, which cannot hold while the summary job itself runs
review fix did not compile: android.speech.tts.Voice has no getLocalizedName() accessor
two named cases failed: voice_selection_returns_to_default assumed the engine voice is unset before the first explicit voice, and rotation_during_speaking failed without observable detail
voice_selection_returns_to_default reported "a fresh handle already selected 'en-US-language'": the framework itself selects the engine default voice while it connects

rotation_during_speaking observed state=SPEAKING started=1 ranges=123 terminal=0: the 900 character request was still being synthesized after the 45 s wait, so the wait was shorter than the real utterance

prior_success.note: the original delivery acceptance with 46 named cases; retained because it is the source the review started from

not_covered: Android host product wiring, background playback, audio focus, media session and haptics
spoken-output quality and latency on a real handset; only engine callbacks, the rendered bytes and the engine's own voice state are evidence
engines other than com.google.android.tts on the acceptance image
a genuine engine-level FAILED terminal event and the Java release failure path; no reliable way to make the installed engine fail mid-utterance
concurrent handles sharing one engine process beyond the eight-handle limit check
the destroy-versus-in-flight-callback window is closed by pinning the handle, but no deterministic in-process reproduction of the old free exists without an ASAN build or a fabricating engine
voice timbre: that the engine really spoke with the selected voice is only observed through the engine's reported current voice, not through the audio content
